statement.p: Find the length of the curve {\bf {r}}{\it(t)}={\bf{i}}\ + 3 {\it t^2} {\bf{j}} + {\it t^3} {\bf{k}}, 0 \le t \le \sqrt{12}

static.solution:
L=\int^{\sqrt{12}}_{0}||\bf r\it'(t)dt||
Differentiating \bf r\it(t) and computing the norm of \bf r\it'(t) gives:
{\bf r}{\it'(t)}=\left\lt 0, 6 t, 3 t^2\right>
||{\bf r}{\it'(t)}||=\sqrt{36 t^2 + 9 t^4}
=t\sqrt{36+9 t^2}, on t\ge 0
Thus,
L=\int^{\sqrt{12}}_0 t\sqrt{36+9 t^2} dt
Integrating (using the substitution u=t^2) we get
L=\left[(36+9 t^2)^{\frac{3}{2}} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{9} \times \frac{1}{2}\right]^{\sqrt{12}}_0
=\frac{1}{27}\left( 144^{\frac{3}{2}}- 36^{\frac{3}{2}} \right)
= 56
